title: Infinitesimal marked automorphisms and normalized vector fields
statement: Let $\Omega$ be an algebraically closed field [def-weil-field, def-weil-algebraic-closure], and let $C$ be a proper connected reduced $\Omega$-scheme of pure dimension one with only nodes [def-weil-proper-morphism, def-weil-connected-scheme, def-pc-reduced-scheme, def-kun-topological-krull-dimension]; a node has completed local ring $\Omega[[u,v]]/(uv)$ [def-weil-pbc-adic-completion, def-weil-pbc-multivariate-power-series]. Let $p_1,\ldots,p_n$ be distinct smooth $\Omega$-points [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms], possibly none. Let $\nu:\widetilde C\to C$ be the normalization [def-weil-pbc-reduced-normalization], and write $\widetilde C=\coprod_a C_a$ for its smooth projective connected components. Put $E_a\subset C_a(\Omega)$ equal to the inverse images of the nodes together with the inverse images of the $p_i$. Let $A$ be the group of automorphisms of $C_{\Omega[\epsilon]/(\epsilon^2)}$ over the dual numbers [def-sc-dual-numbers] that reduce to the identity on $C$ and fix each constant marked section. There is a canonical additive identification $A\cong\bigoplus_a\operatorname{Der}_\Omega(\mathcal O_{C_a},\mathcal O_{C_a};E_a)$. A derivation here is an $\Omega$-linear map of sheaves satisfying the Leibniz rule, and the suffix $E_a$ means that it preserves the ideal sheaf of each point of $E_a$. On a smooth proper connected curve of genus $g$ [def-pc-genus], a nonzero derivation has no such fixed point if $g=1$, has at most two if $g=0$, and cannot exist if $g\ge2$. Consequently $A$ is trivial if $2g(C_a)-2+\#E_a>0$ for every $a$.

source.place: Tags 0E67 (lemma-smooth-vector-fields), 0E68 (lemma-nodal-vector-fields); the infinitesimal identification uses more-morphisms.tex Tag 02H5 (lemma-action-by-derivations). Marked-point restriction is the ideal-preservation condition in the introduction to section-vector-fields.

proof.text: Put $k=\Omega$ and $R=k[\epsilon]/(\epsilon^2)$. On $\mathcal O_C\oplus\epsilon\mathcal O_C$, an $R$-automorphism reducing to the identity is uniquely $a+\epsilon b\mapsto a+\epsilon(b+D(a))$. Multiplicativity is the Leibniz rule and fixing $R$ is $k$-linearity. Conversely this formula glues and has inverse $-D$; it defines local maps since reduction is the identity. Composition adds derivations. Fixing the constant section at $p_i$ says $D(a)(p_i)=0$ for every $a$, equivalently $D(\mathcal I_{p_i})\subseteq\mathcal I_{p_i}$ since $D$ kills $k$. Thus $A$ is the additive group of derivations on $C$ fixing the marked ideals.

source.place: Tag 02H5 (lemma-action-by-derivations), direct verification for the split dual-number thickening; curves.tex section-vector-fields, definition of fixes

proof.text: If $C$ is empty the identification is trivial. Otherwise apply the completed normalization model: there are finitely many smooth projective components, the node set is finite, normalization is an isomorphism off it, and at each node its semilocal normalization ring and completion satisfy exactly the hypotheses of the local descent lemma. All sets $E_a$ are finite.

source.place: Tag 0E68 (lemma-nodal-vector-fields), normalization setup; varieties.tex Tag 0C3V (lemma-normalization-same-after-completion); completed replacement of the uncompleted stalk assertion

proof.text: Apply local derivation descent at every node to extend a derivation of $C$ uniquely to its normalization, fixing both branch points; conversely descend a derivation fixing those branch points. Off nodes use the normalization isomorphism. These local maps glue: in rational-function rings their restrictions are the unique quotient-rule extension, so they agree on overlaps. They are inverse and additive by the same uniqueness. At each smooth marking the isomorphism identifies the two point ideals. Finally a sheaf derivation on a finite disjoint union is a tuple of derivations; the finite product of additive groups equals their direct sum. Together with step 1 this gives the asserted canonical identification.

source.place: Tag 0E68 (lemma-nodal-vector-fields), globalization; section-vector-fields, fixed-point definition; more-algebra.tex Tag 07PE for restriction uniqueness

proof.text: For a smooth proper connected curve, apply the tangent zero-divisor lemma. For every nonzero derivation its fixed points are exactly the support of an effective divisor with degree $2-2g$, each contributing at least one. For $g\ge2$ the negative degree is impossible; for $g=1$ degree zero leaves no fixed point; for $g=0$ degree two permits at most two. This proves all three bounds.

source.place: Tag 0E67 (lemma-smooth-vector-fields), degree argument; Tag 0BS6 (lemma-rr); divisors.tex Tags 02SF and 0BE6, divisor of a rational section

proof.text: The inequality $2g(C_a)-2+\#E_a>0$ requires at least three special points in genus zero and at least one in genus one. The bounds of step 4 therefore kill every summand in step 3, including all genera at least two, and $A$ is trivial. If there are no markings only branch points enter $E_a$; if there are no nodes normalization is an isomorphism, so the construction also covers these cases.
